messages:
Ben Park: Heads-up — after the recent `poetry lock` regen CI started failing across several matrix jobs. Root cause looks like tokenizers went from 0.13.x -> 0.14.0 and some wheels aren't compatible with our alpine builders. Also seeing KMS permission errors in staging tests. Anyone grabbing this?
Maya Lin: Can you paste the failing test log and the pip/poetry output?
Ben Park: sure, here's the pip install snippet from the failing job:
```
Collecting tokenizers==0.14.0
  ERROR: Could not build wheels for tokenizers which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
# fallback tried building from source, failed inside musl container
RuntimeError: rustc version not found
```
Sergio Ramos: That matches: 0.14.0 published wheel targets manylinux2014 but our alpine CI uses musl and tries to build from source. Historically we pinned tokenizers to avoid source builds.
Priya Kapoor: From a security perspective: tokenizers doesn't currently have a CVE, but transformers transitively pulls it. If we pin older wheel we should re-run the dependency CVE scans. Can't regress to a vulnerable version though.
Aisha Malik: On the KMS side, I saw the staging test service account hitting: `PermissionDenied: projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*:cryptoKeyVersions:access` in audit logs. Looks like we lost the `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.view`/`cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign` perms in the test SA role after the last RBAC cleanup.
Ben Park: thanks @Aisha — that's probably why the integration smoke failed. For the tokenizers problem, quick triage options: pin tokenizers to 0.13.3 in the lockfile, add a `manylinux` builder to CI, or force binary-only installs in CI with `--only-binary :all:`. Thoughts?
Maya Lin: pinning lockfile is the fastest to restore CI. We should open a SR for adding a manylinux job long-term. I'll push a branch that pins tokenizers and regen lock.
Sergio Ramos: Agree. Also propose that we add a poetry patch constraint in pyproject to prevent auto-upgrade until we validate wheels. Example patch config: `tokenizers = "^0.13.3"` so future lock regen doesn't float.
Priya Kapoor: Action for security: once pinned, run our vuln scanner (snyk/ossf) against the new lock and verify no CVEs introduced. If any CVE shows up, we need to escalate to patch prioritization — but likely fine. Also confirm KMS perms change in staging isn't applied to prod.
Aisha Malik: I'll restore the minimal KMS role for the staging SA and add a short runbook entry: steps to validate `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` and the two bindings we need.
ci-bot: Build #artifacts/job-342 failed: see https://ci.redwood.dev/342 (tokenizers wheel build error).
devops-bot: Deploy staging aborted due to KMS permission error (error id e7c1).
Ben Park: Plan: 1) Maya to open PR pinning tokenizers -> 0.13.3 and regen lock (hotfix), 2) Aisha to restore KMS perms in staging + run IAM audit, 3) Priya to run vuln scan on updated lockfile, 4) Sergio to add poetry patch constraint and an issue to add manylinux test matrix. I'll create Jira tickets and link them here. Ping me if you need access to the broken job artifacts. :thumbsup:
Maya Lin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5912 — hotfix pin + lock regen. CI rerun queued.
Ben Park: thanks team — marking as triaged, will follow up on the vuln scan results and the RBAC audit.
